name: IMD BharatFS
architecture: High-resolution global physical numerical weather prediction
description: India-developed 6 km global forecast system with strong relevance to monsoon evaluation.
access: Public forecast plots are available; a versioned machine-readable raw archive was not verified.
pros: Fine global grid is relevant to coastal and terrain-sensitive comparisons
cons: Raw issued forecast archive access needs confirmation
Grid spacing does not establish local extreme-rain skill

use_context.region: Global forecast with direct relevance to India; prioritize coastal and Western Ghats verification sites.
use_context.season: All seasons; monsoon and dry-season calibration should be reported separately.
use_context.lead: Operational short-to-medium-range candidate; compare equal valid times and pinned issue cycles.
use_context.weather: Rainfall, heat and wind guidance; assess intense monsoon rain against independent gauges.
use_context.analysis: BharatFS is a valuable India-provider anchor for the atlas. It is not connected to Anvaya X's live feed or trained router. Before it receives any blend weight, obtain timestamped raw forecasts, confirm variables and accumulation windows, then test independently at matched Indian observation sites.

name: NOAA AIGFS
description: NOAA's operational AI global deterministic guidance, distinct from older GraphCastGFS archives.
access: Operational NOAA product listings; issued archive ingestion is not implemented in Anvaya X.
pros: Useful physical-versus-AI comparator when issue cycles match
cons: Deterministic trajectory needs separate uncertainty calibration
Do not transfer skill claims from older GraphCastGFS versions

use_context.region: Global product can cover Indian locations; local station and rain-gauge verification remains essential.
use_context.season: Year-round candidate, with separate Southwest-monsoon and dry-season checks.
use_context.lead: Short through extended medium range; compare the exact six-hourly valid times and issue cycles.
use_context.weather: Large-scale rain, heat and wind patterns; localized extremes need calibration and spatial checks.
use_context.analysis: AIGFS adds an operational AI family to a physical-model comparison. It is not yet fetched by this site's live desk, nor fitted into the research gate. Archive issue and publication times before training; do not treat shared initialization or model lineage as independent evidence of skill.

name: NOAA AIGEFS
description: Multiple AI forecast members for probabilistic global guidance.
access: NOAA operational product listings; member archive ingestion is not implemented here.
pros: Member-level scenarios can support event probabilities
cons: Shared AI lineage creates correlated errors
HGEFS already includes AIGEFS and GEFS, so avoid double counting

use_context.region: Global ensemble available over India; assess reliability by terrain and coastal regime.
use_context.season: All seasons; test monsoon heavy-rain calibration independently from dry-season events.
use_context.lead: Medium-range uncertainty guidance where complete, time-matched member archives exist.
use_context.weather: Heavy-rain, heat and high-wind event probabilities after local reliability assessment.
use_context.analysis: AIGEFS is a candidate probabilistic AI expert, not a current Anvaya X input. Its full member distribution may add information that a deterministic AI run cannot. HGEFS is a combination of AIGEFS and GEFS, so treating all three as independent blend experts would overstate source diversity.

name: FuXi 2.1
architecture: RoPE-conditioned Swin transformer with variable-aware decoder
description: Open research checkpoint producing 0.25° global fields at six-hour steps to ten days.
access: Downloadable research weights and inference code; no verified live forecast feed here.
pros: Precipitation and near-surface wind are native outputs
cons: Published extreme-event comparison covers limited sample cases

use_context.region: Global grid includes India, but no Mumbai or India-specific advantage has been established here.
use_context.season: Year-round research candidate; fine-tune or calibrate monsoon and non-monsoon periods separately.
use_context.lead: Six-hourly steps to 240 hours; preserve the six-hour precipitation accumulation semantics.
use_context.weather: Heavy rain and strong wind structure are research motivations; validate each threshold locally.
use_context.analysis: FuXi 2.1 is technically attractive because its published checkpoint includes precipitation, temperature and 10 m wind fields. The model card itself limits its extreme-event scorecard to sample cases. To use it in the blend, run its exact checkpoint on archived initial states, align six-hour intervals, and test against independent India observations.

name: DWD ICON Global
description: Open global physical guidance with forecast GRIB files for surface and upper-air fields.
access: Live open GRIB directories; versioned archive and decoding still need integration.
cons: GRIB field and interval decoding is required
No locally measured superiority is implied by resolution

use_context.region: Global coverage includes India; compare Western Ghats and coastal points against observations.
use_context.season: Year-round physical comparator with monsoon-specific bias and reliability analysis.
use_context.lead: Short-to-medium range; use only leads shared by all comparator sources.
use_context.weather: Synoptic rain, near-surface heat and wind; convection-scale extremes need local verification.
use_context.analysis: ICON Global can improve ensemble diversity because it is a separate physical modeling system from GFS and IFS. Its public GRIB files are a realistic integration route, but operational use still requires a historical archive, cycle timestamps, unit conversion and calibrated error estimates.

name: DWD ICON-EPS Global
description: Open ICON ensemble members that can support probabilistic weather scenarios.
access: Live open GRIB member directories; matched archive is not connected.
pros: Member spread can inform event uncertainty
cons: Shares modeling lineage with ICON control
Lead and cycle availability differ; verify exact product schedule

use_context.region: Global coverage includes India; coarse ensemble grid still needs gauge-scale assessment.
use_context.season: All seasons with independent monsoon and dry-season reliability diagrams.
use_context.lead: Short-to-medium range within the exact available run and member horizon.
use_context.weather: Heavy-rain, heat and wind scenarios where ensemble members provide a calibrated distribution.
use_context.analysis: ICON-EPS is an uncertainty source rather than a guaranteed better deterministic forecast. When ICON control and ICON-EPS appear together, their common model lineage must be accounted for. Verify member completeness and event reliability before assigning them simultaneous weights.

name: ECCC GDPS Hybrid
architecture: GEM atmosphere-ocean physical model with large-scale spectral nudging toward GEML AI
description: Operational global hybrid that couples physical dynamics with AI guidance for large-scale temperature and wind.
access: Public GDPS 15 km products via ECCC Datamart and GeoMet; not fetched by this site.
cons: GEML-guided and GDPS output errors are dependent
Rainfall remains a physical-model output requiring local evaluation

use_context.region: Global 15 km atmospheric guidance covers India, including coastal and inland regions.
use_context.season: All seasons; evaluate monsoon precipitation and heat separately before blending.
use_context.lead: Two runs daily to ten days; align cycles and valid times with other candidates.
use_context.weather: Large-scale rain, heat and wind patterns; local convective rain still needs observation checks.
use_context.analysis: GDPS is a particularly instructive hybrid: GEM dynamics are nudged toward GEML's AI large-scale temperature and horizontal winds. It is not an independent GEML-plus-GDPS pair, and its precipitation must not be described as a direct GEML forecast. Anvaya X does not currently ingest this product.

name: ECCC GEPS
description: Public Canadian global ensemble guidance with member-level uncertainty fields.
access: Open ECCC Datamart products; historical member archive matching is pending.
cons: Coarse global grid cannot resolve city-scale rainfall
Calibrating a member distribution requires matched observations

use_context.region: Global ensemble includes India, but city and terrain effects are unresolved at coarse scale.
use_context.season: All seasons; assess monsoon event reliability separately from winter and pre-monsoon heat.
use_context.lead: Medium-range ensemble guidance up to the documented product horizon.
use_context.weather: Probabilistic rain, heat and wind guidance after threshold-specific calibration.
use_context.analysis: GEPS adds a separate ensemble-provider family and can expose scenario spread when deterministic models disagree. Its open product route does not by itself supply a verified Indian skill archive. Preserve member IDs, forecast cycles and valid intervals for honest evaluation.
